category_title: Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder experiencing psychomotor retardation, cognitive disorganization, and emotional volatility
minimal_context: The student is working on Algebra II problems from a textbook on a whiteboard during a one-on-one session at home.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at the next Algebra II problem from the textbook. Please solve it on the whiteboard.

STUDENT: (Holds very still and is slow to reach out for a pencil) I get it. I can work while you’re here.

TUTOR: Okay, go ahead and write out your steps.

STUDENT: (Moves at about half-speed through the algebra work, struggling to translate the book examples to the book problems, and makes a calculation error)

TUTOR: Your answer is incorrect. Look at your calculations and try reworking it.

STUDENT: (Gets bogged down and spends an extended period reworking the calculation error, circling around and around and not seeing an escape) Why bother?

options.A: Create an assignment sheet with the Algebra II task broken into subtasks, each with a check-off box, dividing the textbook problems into subsets of no more than six problems.
options.B: Point to an additional Algebra II problem, sliding a finger out from the corner of the textbook page.
options.C: Terminate the academic demands and remove the textbook and whiteboard from the student's workspace for 10 seconds.
options.D: Deliver verbal statements or gestures (e.g., high five, thumbs up) indicating approval beyond simple acknowledgment of the student's work on the whiteboard.
